Strike · Bulgaria

CONTSHIP JET struck by surface drones offshore; crew rescued, ship later sank

28 October 2026 · CONTSHIP JET off Cape Kaliakra · Reported maritime-drone strike

Surface-drone strike reported by authorities; all 18 crew rescued; subsequent sinking confirmed by Varna Radio

Bulgarian defence authorities say Navy surveillance and a French patrol aircraft observed a surface-drone attack on CONTSHIP JET at 12:00 local (10:00 UTC) on 28 October, with three hits observed. Varna Radio gives the strike position as 43°15′N, 028°48′E off Cape Kaliakra. This is one offshore merchant-shipping occurrence, not a confirmed Bulgarian territorial incursion.

Defence and transport authorities confirm all 18 crew were rescued. Varna Radio NAVWARN 768/26 confirms the ship subsequently sank at 20:30 UTC on 28 October at 43°07.80′N, 028°45.36′E, with more than 20 containers drifting, including dangerous goods. This supersedes the earlier unofficial sinking report.

The drone operator, launch origin and motive remain unknown. Reuters reports Ambrey’s provisional video-based assessment of a likely Murena-300S-derived design; this is not a confirmed model or operator identification. Three reported drones and three observed hits are not separate incidents. The later sinking position does not replace the original strike coordinate.

Navigation warnings on 1 November reported drifting containers near Burgas Bay. BNR linked four of them to CONTSHIP JET only provisionally; the official notices do not name their source vessel. These are hazard follow-ups, not new attacks or a cumulative container count.

Attribution and uncertainty

Origin / operator / attribution
Drone operator, launch origin and motive remain unresolved. Reuters on 29 October reported Ambrey analyst Tomas Alexa’s provisional assessment that the filmed surface drone likely derives from the Russian Murena-300S design; this is not a confirmed model or operator attribution.
Investigation / uncertainty
The official observation account and navigation warning support the attack, location and rescue, not a technical model or operator identification. Ambrey’s video-based design assessment reported by Reuters remains provisional. The minister reported three maritime drones, while the defence ministry describes three observed hits; neither creates separate occurrences. Operator, launch point and motive remain unknown. The sinking is confirmed by NAVWARN 768/26, but its later position is not the strike location. Neither the wreck nor cargo drift establishes a new drone incursion. The Burgas sightings are not a unique additive container total; vessel association remains provisional and no new pollution finding is established.

Full record

Strike

Red Strike for reported damaging maritime-drone attack. Offshore context explicitly separated from confirmed territorial incursions.

Anchor updated to the reported strike coordinate in Varna Radio NAVWARN 759/26 (43°15′N, 028°48′E), replacing the preliminary editorial anchor. Earlier reports gave about 16 nautical miles from Kaliakra or 21 nautical miles from Shabla. Offshore coverage is not a confirmed sovereign-territory incursion; later drift or sinking positions are not strike coordinates. NAVWARN 768/26 places the subsequent sinking at 43°07.80′N, 028°45.36′E; this does not replace the original strike anchor.

Map positions are approximate anchors for the named place, not verified incident coordinates.

Reported date
28 October 2026, 10:00 UTC (12:00 Bulgarian local time)
Record type
reported_offshore_drone_strike
Date basis
Varna Radio NAVWARN 759/26 dates the surface-drone hit to 10:00 UTC on 28 October; the defence ministry gives 12:00 local. These are the reported strike time, not publication timestamps.
Location / jurisdiction
Black Sea southeast of Cape Kaliakra in Varna Radio’s warning. Varna Radio NAVWARN 759/26 reports the strike at 43°15′N, 028°48′E; the defence ministry describes 17 miles east of the cape.
Event categories
Reported maritime-drone strike on merchant shipping; crew abandonment
What was reported
The Bulgarian defence ministry says the Navy surveillance system and a French patrol aircraft observed the surface-drone attack at 12:00 local on 28 October and three hits were observed. Varna Radio NAVWARN 759/26 identifies CONTSHIP JET and reports a surface-drone hit at 10:00 UTC. Included under the register’s existing offshore merchant-shipping treatment, not as a confirmed Bulgarian territorial incursion.
Aircraft / vessel / quantity
Liberian-flagged container ship CONTSHIP JET, IMO 9348625. Bulgarian defence minister reports three maritime drones; precise platform type/model unestablished.
Origin / operator / attribution
Drone operator, launch origin and motive remain unresolved. Reuters on 29 October reported Ambrey analyst Tomas Alexa’s provisional assessment that the filmed surface drone likely derives from the Russian Murena-300S design; this is not a confirmed model or operator attribution.
Damage / casualties / disruption
All 18 crew were rescued according to Bulgarian defence and transport authorities, corroborating the earlier manager account. Varna Radio NAVWARN 768/26 confirms CONTSHIP JET sank at 20:30 UTC on 28 October at 43°07.80′N, 028°45.36′E. More than 20 containers were adrift, with flammable gases and liquids and other dangerous goods among the lost cargo. This official warning supersedes the earlier explicitly unconfirmed sinking report.
Response / outcome
The transport ministry reports an alert at 12:01 local and abandonment at 12:13 on 28 October; at 12:53 eight crew were aboard a Navy cutter and ten in a lifeboat. The defence ministry says three naval ships deployed immediately and all 18 crew were rescued by 13:45 local. These official accounts supersede reliance on the manager-only safety statement. Eftimov told bTV that the Navy had warned ships in the area roughly half an hour before the attack. On 1 November NAVWARN779 reported four containers east of Burgas Bay at 08:55 UTC; NAVWARN780 reported a container at 12:20 UTC. BNR described the four as probably from CONTSHIP JET, but the notices themselves do not identify a vessel.
Investigation / uncertainty
The official observation account and navigation warning support the attack, location and rescue, not a technical model or operator identification. Ambrey’s video-based design assessment reported by Reuters remains provisional. The minister reported three maritime drones, while the defence ministry describes three observed hits; neither creates separate occurrences. Operator, launch point and motive remain unknown. The sinking is confirmed by NAVWARN 768/26, but its later position is not the strike location. Neither the wreck nor cargo drift establishes a new drone incursion. The Burgas sightings are not a unique additive container total; vessel association remains provisional and no new pollution finding is established.
Route / entry mechanism
Reported voyage from Haifa, Israel, toward Constanța, Romania. Admiral Emil Eftimov told bTV on 29 October that the drones approached from the east over the sea; precise track and launch point remain unknown.
Explosive payload
Unknown; no separately established explosion count.
Counting / links
One CONTSHIP JET occurrence, distinct from KHORYV, CHELSEA 3 and earlier ship attacks. Three reported drones, impacts and abandonment are not separate event records.
